# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 32 MISS WINIFRED DISCUSSES THE AFFAIR

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“And are you saying, Nell, dearie, that Rufus Vane has actually proven to be someone else entirely instead of Rufus Vane? Is THAT the reason you called me earlier today?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0000 }

“Indeed, Miss Winifred. It is quite astonishing, isn’t it?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0001 }

“It’s—it’s—just like a man,” Miss Winifred stammered weakly. Her hands shook as she removed her hat. Never before had Miss Winifred been so completely overwhelmed.
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0002 }

“Nell, it seems I am unable to feel it,” she remarked. “I have listened to you state it—and I trust your word—yet I am unable to grasp it. Rufus Vane has passed away—he has been deceased throughout all these years—and Lorna is no longer bound?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0003 }

“Yes. Freedom has come to her through the truth. That line was the most magnificent in the Bible, just as Hugh remarked.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0004 }

“Relate the entire story, Nell, dearie. Ever since receiving your call I’ve been completely baffled, believe ME. Winifred Tolley has never felt so kerflummuxed until now.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0005 }

“There is not much to relate. Lorna wrote a brief letter. She omitted the details. Laurence Vane—this man—has regained his memory and realizes his identity. He states that Rufus contracted yellow fever in Cuba, forcing the Four Sisters to depart in his absence. Laurence remained to care for him. However, he passed away soon after.
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0006 }

“The reason Laurence refrained from writing to Lorna was his plan to return home immediately and speak to her in person.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0007 }

“And what kept him from doing so?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0008 }

“I think his mishap probably got in the way. Hugh mentions that Laurence Vane might very well have no memory of his mishap, or the events preceding it, and perhaps won't ever recall it. Its occurrence was likely shortly following the passing of Rufus. Once Lorna sends another letter, we might discover additional details.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0009 }

“Is it stated what her plans are? What is the date of her return home?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0010 }

“She states that she intends to remain beside Laurence Vane up to the point when he is able to depart from the hospital. A letter has been sent by her to his relatives in Nova Scotia. It appears that the sole close family member Laurence has is an elder sister who is married. That sister was still alive at the time Laurence embarked aboard the Four Sisters, though naturally it is uncertain to us what might have occurred in the intervening time. Have you at any time met Laurence Vane, Miss Winifred?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0011 }

“I did. Everything is returning to my mind. Eighteen years back, when he and Rufus must have been roughly seventeen, he stayed here to visit his Uncle Abner. You see, they were double cousins. Their mothers were twin sisters and their fathers were brothers, so they possessed a striking resemblance to one another. Naturally,” Miss Winifred appended with scorn, “this wasn't a case of those weird likenesses written about in stories where a pair of individuals are so identical that they can take each other's spots without their closest loved ones knowing the difference. Back then, provided you observed them side by side and close by, you could distinguish easily enough between Laurence and Rufus. When separated, or at a bit of a distance, telling them apart was harder. Those two scamps pulled many pranks on folks and considered it big entertainment. Laurence Vane stood slightly taller and considerably plumper than Rufus—even if neither could be deemed truly fat—for both belonged to the slim sort. Rufus possessed a cheek color higher than Laurence, along with hair a shade paler. Yet their facial traits were identical, and each shared that strange ocular quirk—one hazel eye and one blue. Outside of that, they didn't share many similarities. Although Laurence was a rascal for pranks, he was a genuinely pleasant guy, even if some claimed he enjoyed a drink even back then. Still, everyone preferred him over Rufus. He stayed in these parts for about a month. Lorna didn't ever see him; she was merely eight or nine at the time, and I recall now that the entire winter was spent by her across the harbor with her grandmother West. Captain Saul was absent as well—it was during that winter that he suffered a shipwreck on the Magdalens. I doubt that he or Lorna had ever been told about the cousin from Nova Scotia resembling Rufus so closely. Not a soul gave him a thought when Captain Saul escorted Rufus—I mean to say, Laurence—back home. Naturally, the rest of us believed Rufus had undergone a major transformation—he had grown so heavy and stocky. However, we attributed that to his ordeal, which was undoubtedly the cause, because, as I previously mentioned, Laurence wasn't heavy initially either. Furthermore, there existed no other clue for us to divine the truth, since the person's mind was completely vanished. I fail to see how our collective deception is at all surprising. Even so, it is a shocking realization. And Lorna gave up her finest years taking care of an individual who possessed no right to her devotion! Oh, curse the men! Whatever action they take, it turns out wrong. And regardless of their identity, they turn out to be someone they ought not to be. They truly irritate me.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0012 }

“Hugh and Captain Saul are men, and the truth has finally been uncovered because of them,” Nell said.
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0013 }

“Well, I grant that,” Miss Winifred gave in with hesitation. “My harsh words to the doctor make me sorry now. Never before in my life have I experienced shame over something I uttered to a man. Even so, I doubt that I will admit it to him. He will simply be forced to assume it. Well, Nell, my dear, we are blessed that the Lord fails to grant every prayer we make. Continuously and fervently, I have prayed that Rufus would not be healed by the surgery. Naturally, I refrained from stating it in such direct terms. Nevertheless, that thought resided at the rear of my consciousness, and I am certain the Lord recognized it.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0014 }

“Indeed, He has granted the essence of what you prayed for. Your genuine desire was that circumstances would not become more difficult for Lorna. I fear that within my private thoughts I had been wishing for the procedure to fail, a feeling for which I am properly disgraced.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0015 }

“In what way does Lorna appear to handle it?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0016 }

“Her writing resembles that of someone stunned. It is my belief that she scarcely comprehends it so far, just as we do not. Her sole mention of her own person consists of the statement, 'It all seems like a strange dream to me, Nell.’”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0017 }

“Poor child! I imagine that once a prisoner’s chains are removed, he would feel strange and disoriented without them at first. Nell, dearie, there is an idea that keeps entering my head. What about Adrian Treleaven? Both of us are aware that Lorna cared for him. Did you ever consider that he might have cared for her?”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0018 }

“It—did—once,” conceded Nell, believing she could say that much.
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0019 }

“Indeed, there was no cause for me to believe he was, yet it simply seemed to my mind that he HAD to be. Look here, Nell, dearie, God is my witness that I am no match-maker, and I hold every act of that nature in contempt. Even so, were I in your shoes and composing a letter to that Treleaven fellow, I would merely bring up, in a passing way, the recent occurrence. That is precisely how I would act.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0020 }

“Naturally, I am going to bring it up in my letter to him,” Nell remarked, speaking somewhat coldly. For some reason, Miss Winifred was not a person with whom she could converse about this matter. Even so, she was forced to acknowledge that this very idea had been secretly present in her own thoughts from the moment she learned Lorna was free. However, she refused to cheapen it through open conversation.
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0021 }

“Naturally, there isn't any huge hurry, dearie. However, thirteen years have passed since Rufus Vane died, and Lorna has spent a sufficient portion of her existence on him. We shall simply observe the outcome. Regarding Laurence Vane, who departed and then returned from the dead when his death and end were universally assumed, exactly as a man would do, I feel genuinely bad for him. He will appear out of place everywhere.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0022 }

“Given that he remains young, he will have the capacity to establish his position once more, provided he achieves a full recovery, which appears probable. The situation must feel exceedingly peculiar to the unfortunate man. It seems to me that the entire duration following his mishap will be a blank to him.”
{: #nw-v04-c32-p0023 }
